w:r.w:t: This audit covers every page of the Unsocials Thailand website across five dimensions: content accuracy, messaging consistency, design quality, technical functionality, and conversion optimisation. The site has strong bones - the concept, brand voice, and case study content are genuinely compelling. However, there are critical inconsistencies that undermine credibility and several broken or placeholder elements that reduce trust.

The biggest risk: a potential client in Thailand who lands on this site will find contradictions (Bangkok vs Pattaya), missing social links, placeholder widgets, and inconsistent numbers. These are fixable in under a week and should be treated as urgent.
These 8 issues will directly cost you clients if not fixed immediately. A prospect doing due diligence will find all of these within 5 minutes.
Says 'BANGKOK BUILT' throughout About page - you are based in Pattaya, not Bangkok
Change to 'PATTAYA BASED' in ticker and all About page references
Footer says 'Bangkok - Thailand'. Copyright says 2025 not 2026
Change to 'Pattaya - Thailand' and update copyright to 2026 on all pages
About page says '1M+ THB Revenue Generated' but homepage says '50M+ THB Generated' - a 50x difference that destroys credibility
Decide on ONE number and use it everywhere. Recommended: '50M+ THB Revenue Generated for Clients'
Social links (Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, WhatsApp) all go to '#' - completely broken
Add real URLs to all social platforms immediately
Client review profile photos use Ava and Alex (AI characters) - looks fabricated to any visitor
Replace with real client logos, hotel thumbnails, or simple monogram initials
LightWidget placeholder text is visible to all website visitors - not connected
Connect real LightWidget feed or remove section until it is live
All 6 case study cards link to work.html - clicking any of them goes nowhere new
Build individual pages or anchor sections for each case study
Quote attribution says 'UNSOCIALS Thailand - Bangkok' at the bottom of the About page
The hero tagline 'We Don't Do Social. We Dominate It.' is bold and memorable - keep it. The supporting content has inconsistencies to fix.
Founded in India 2020 - Now in Pattaya, Thailand - 100+ Global Brands
Founded in India 2020 - Expanding Across Southeast Asia - 100+ Global Brands
'50M+ THB Generated' on homepage vs '1M+ THB Revenue Generated' on About page
Align to one number everywhere. Use '50M+ THB in Revenue Generated for Clients' if accurate
Case study shows '+10L In 60 Days' using Indian Rupee symbol (Rs) on a Thailand-focused site
Replace with THB or use a metric like '+286% Direct Bookings in 60 Days'
This is your single biggest differentiator. No agency in Thailand is doing this. The messaging currently undersells it.
'The Unfair Advantage. AI Talent. Zero Production Cost. Infinite Output.'
'Our AI representatives, Ava and Alex, aren't just faces. They are the core of our creative engine...'

'Meet Ava and Alex - Unsocials' proprietary AI brand talent. They shoot every day, never cancel, never age, and cost a fraction of a traditional production. Your brand's unfair advantage - available now.'
Location: Homepage - Ava and Alex description
IMPORTANT: Be transparent that Ava and Alex are AI. The current phrasing is slightly ambiguous. Thai clients will respect the honesty - hiding it risks backlash and trust issues.
AI character images (Ava and Alex) used as reviewer profile photos
Use real client logos, brand thumbnails, or monogram initials on coloured circles. Never use AI characters as real people reviews.
Review exists but has no specific result - just general positive sentiment
Add a result: 'In 30 days, our direct booking rate increased by 40%.' Adding numbers makes testimonials 3x more credible.
'Trusted by 40+ brands across 8 countries' vs '100+ Global Brands' shown elsewhere
Use '100+ Global Brands' consistently. Remove '40+' - it makes the bigger number look wrong.
'We transform your channels from a afterthought into...'
'We transform your channels from an afterthought into...' (simple grammar fix)
Location: Services - Grammar error in Service 02
'10x Average increase in organic engagement' with no timeframe
'10x Average increase in organic engagement within 90 days across active clients'
'We generate perfection in a vacuum' - confusing phrasing
'We generate studio-quality visuals in days, not weeks. No crew, no location, no delays.'
'A tight team of strategists, creators and digital natives built in Bangkok.'
'A tight team of strategists, creators and digital natives - born in Jaipur, operating in Pattaya.'
'PATTAYA BASED - RESULTS DRIVEN - DIGITAL NATIVES - OBSESSED - PERFORMANCE FIRST - INEVITABLE'
'50+ Brands Worked With Across Thailand' - contradicts '100+ Global Brands' on homepage
'100+ Brands Worked With Globally' - must match the homepage figure exactly
'We live here. We understand the culture, the travellers, the expats' - vague
'We live and operate in Pattaya. Our founder moved from Jaipur to build this - not as outsiders, but as people who chose Thailand as home. That difference shows in every campaign.'
All 6 case study cards link to work.html - clicking any goes nowhere new. A big red flag for serious clients.
Build individual pages: /work/elysium.html, /work/alexa.html etc. This is the most important conversion fix on the site.
Location: Work - All case study links
Cards show client name and services but no result headline on the card
Add one headline metric to each card: 'Elysium Pattaya - +286% Direct Bookings'. Results on the card drive clicks.
Location: Work - Missing result metrics on cards
'GPS Gems - Brand Identity - AI Content - Organic Growth Strategy' - no location, no result
'GPS Gems Thailand - 3x Engagement Growth - Bangkok' - add specifics to every card
Location: Work - GPS Gems case study
Homepage navbar appears TWICE in the HTML - code duplication bug. Remove one instance.
Services and About pages are missing 'Home' in the nav - add it for consistent navigation across all pages.
The EN/TH language toggle exists but Thai version does not appear to be live. Either build Thai version or remove toggle until ready - a non-functional toggle looks broken.
'Book a Call' CTA goes to WhatsApp on homepage but to contact.html on Services page. Standardise to WhatsApp everywhere - it converts better.
Reel videos (r1 to r4) in the hero are excellent. Verify they autoplay on mobile - many browsers block mobile autoplay. Add a static poster image fallback.
'INITIALISING' loading screen is a cool effect but if it takes over 1.5 seconds it frustrates mobile users. Reduce animation duration or add a progress bar.
'Scroll' indicator at the bottom of the hero is good UX. Make it a bouncing animated arrow to draw more attention.
The yellow star rating (5 stars) is good. But the profile images (AI characters) undercut authenticity completely.
Replace Ava and Alex profile images with: real client logos, hotel exterior photos, or simple monogram initials on a coloured circle background.
The Xperience Stays review has no actual result mentioned - just sentiment. Add a number. Any number.
Ticker/marquee animations need testing on iOS Safari - these commonly break on Apple devices.
Contact form has no visible validation states. Add real-time validation and a clear success message so users know their submission worked.
Google Maps embed uses generic Pattaya coordinates - update to your exact office pin location.
The case study cards on work.html have an arrow (up-right) implying clickthrough to detail. Since nothing happens, either make them work or remove the arrow.
Thai and Indian clients have the same 10 questions before signing. Answering on-site saves hours of sales calls.
Min budget, contract terms, results timeline, AI disclosure, languages spoken, reporting frequency
'Book a Call' is the only CTA. Even a 'Starting from 15,000 THB/month' helps clients self-qualify.
3 tiers: Starter / Growth / Full Scale. Show inclusions. Add 'Custom' option with inquiry CTA.
SEO is near zero right now. Monthly blog on Thailand digital marketing would rank for client search terms.
Example posts: How Hotels in Pattaya Can Reduce OTA Dependence, AI Content for Thailand Hospitality 2026
'We have a small, obsessive team' but who are they? Faces = trust. Especially in Thailand where relationships are everything.
Founder photo, role, brief background. Even 3-4 people with photos transforms trust levels significantly.
Position Unsocials as the expert voice on Thailand digital. Data page with stats and tourism numbers.
Builds SEO and positions you as an authority before the client even reads your case studies.
Not present anywhere on the site. A WhatsApp bubble converts Thai clients instantly.
Floating WhatsApp icon bottom-right on all pages. Link to +66960531394 with a pre-filled message.
The site has almost no SEO setup. For a performance marketing agency, this is ironic - and very fixable quickly.
Homepage title: 'UNSOCIALS - We Make It Inevitable' has zero keywords. Change to: 'Unsocials Thailand | Digital Marketing Agency in Pattaya'
About page has no meta description tag at all - this page will not rank for anything
Services page missing meta description. Add: 'Performance marketing, social media management, and AI creative for hotels, beach clubs and brands in Thailand. Based in Pattaya.'
Work page has a meta description - good. Lead with Thailand keywords first for local SEO.
'Digital marketing agency Pattaya' - currently zero content targeting this specific term
'Hotel marketing Thailand' - your strongest niche, build a dedicated landing page around it
'Social media agency Bangkok' - secondary market, worth a landing page for Bangkok leads
'AI content agency Thailand' - you are first mover here, own this term before competitors arrive
'Reduce OTA commissions Thailand' - very high commercial intent search from hotel decision makers
Fix in this exact order. Week 1 items are all quick fixes - most take under 30 minutes each.
Fix ALL Bangkok references to Pattaya across About page, Services footer, and About footer
Update copyright year from 2025 to 2026 on Services and About pages
Replace AI character photos in testimonials with client logos or monogram initials
Connect all social media links in footer: Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, WhatsApp
Connect LightWidget Instagram feed or remove the placeholder section entirely
Fix the duplicated navbar in homepage HTML (two nav bars in the code)
Align all revenue stats to one consistent number across every single page
Remove Indian Rupee symbol from case study - replace with THB equivalent or percentage metric
Fix grammar: 'from a afterthought' to 'from an afterthought' on Services page
Add WhatsApp floating button to every page on the site
Build individual case study pages for all 6 clients with full breakdown, metrics, and visuals
Add result metric badges to all case study cards on the work page
Build a basic FAQ page (a single accordion page is enough to start)
Fix Google Maps embed to use your actual Pattaya office coordinates and pin
Add Home link to navigation on all inner pages: Services, About, Work, Contact
Standardise 'Book a Call' CTA button to WhatsApp across all pages
Write and publish first 3 blog posts targeting your priority SEO keywords
Build a Pricing / Packages page with at least 3 tiers and starting price points
Add a Team section to the About page with real photos and names
Build a Thailand Market Stats page to establish digital authority in the market
Either launch the Thai language version fully or remove the EN/TH toggle until it is ready
Add meta descriptions and keyword-optimised page titles to all 5 pages

The brand voice is strong. We Make It Inevitable is a great tagline. Case studies are real and impressive. The AI creative angle with Ava and Alex is a genuine differentiator - no agency in Thailand is doing this. Visual design is premium and appropriate for the market.

The site undermines its own credibility with inconsistent data, broken links, wrong city names, and placeholder content. A hotel GM in Pattaya doing a 10-minute check before calling will find these issues and lose confidence. Entirely fixable - treat as highest priority this week.

With Week 1 fixes alone, this site goes from startup to serious agency. Month 1 additions including blog, individual case study pages, pricing, and team section will make it a lead-generating machine. The bones are excellent. Execution just needs to catch up to the ambition.
